Found underneath a flat flagstone in my backyard. Habitat is suburban and the flagstone was near the edge of our lawn. Multiple of this species were found with a colony of what I assume to be Tetramorium immigrans, although these individuals were much smaller than the T. immigrans.

There's been a lot of ant activity in this particular spot within the past week. I really wish I knew what was happening because it appears to be an all-out war.

(Please forgive my lack of knowledge and aptitude of ants.)

So the past several days in the late afternoon I've seen these -- what I'm assuming are -- pharaoh ant queens. I have no idea where they came from and have never seen their small but mighty counterparts until today. Some queens were crawling around while others appeared to be dying.

Today, while there were even more queens out, the most tiniest, cutest, light-orange ants started coming out of this hole. Enter pharaoh ants. They appeared to be stinging and fighting with another species of ant (which I'm going to naively call carpenter ants). Those guys have been living there for awhile.

So what it appears to be is the pharaoh ant is trying to take over the carpenter ants. Because the more the pharaoh ants would sting the poor convulsing carpenter ants, the more troops they would send for backup.

I apologize for the poor quality pictures, but if any ant-savvy individuals know what's happening, I'd certainly be intrigued to know. I must've spent a good 20 minutes watching them.
